title: Sentinel reconcile-unblock and graceful upgrade resume for stalled on-prem tenant upgrades
creator: Asha Patel
description: Several on-prem customers experienced tenant upgrades stuck in 'post-install-hook' state when Helm hooks timeout or the nodeagent pod is OOMKilled during preflight. The operator backlog causes reconciliation to stall and CRs to remain half-applied, leading to config drift (Secrets/Finalizers/HelmRelease status) and blocking future upgrades. This ticket implements a sentinel that detects orphaned helm release states and a safe unblock flow that re-enables reconciliation, repairs finalizers where safe, and resumes a staged upgrade. It also codifies an emergency runbook for SRE and Solutions Engineers to follow during escalations.
problem_statement: Upgrades can stall indefinitely when Helm post-install hooks never complete or the operator loses watch state. Current manual remediation is error-prone: customers have seen missing finalizers, secret mismatches, and drifted ConfigMaps. We need an automated and auditable way to detect these conditions, minimally repair node-local state, and resume upgrades without data loss or broad rollbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Automated sentinel metric 'upgrade_stalled_sentinel{tenant}' emitted to prometheus when HelmRelease state is >15m in post-install-hook
Controller library exposes a ReconcileUnblock API gated by a safety checklist (no in-flight DB migrations, no locked user jobs)
Safe hotpatch that can reattach operator watches and requeue HelmRelease reconciliation without deleting user secrets
A validated runbook with play-by-play commands that an SRE can execute in <30 minutes to recover a tenant and record actions
Two customer recovery drills completed in staging; observability dashboard shows TTL for stalled upgrades reduced to <5m for 90% of cases after rollout
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Add detection — reconcile loop emits metrics for HelmRelease phase lifetimes and records a tenant-scoped 'stalled' annotation
Phase 2: Safe unblock operator endpoint — implement controller command to replay Helm post-install hooks idempotently and rehydrate KV cache if missing
Phase 3: Hotpatch release — lightweight operator image (patch bump) that adds a safe-repair path for finalizers and resumes reconciliation
Phase 4: Runbook and drills — document step-by-step recovery, test with two non-production tenants and one canary customer on Dedicated
Phase 5: Telemetry dashboards & alerting — PagerDuty escalation, runbook link in alert, and postmortem templates
tech_decisions: Use annotations on HelmRelease objects rather than adding new CRDs to minimize cluster-wide upgrades
Prefer idempotent replay of Helm hooks instead of deleting and reapplying releases to avoid secret churn
Expose unblock via controller-tenant-scoped REST subresource, require audit logging and a two-person confirmation in the runbook for production
Limit automated repairs to non-destructive actions; destructive steps (force delete helm release / secret re-seed) remain manual and gated behind customer approval
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Automated replay could trigger duplicate side-effects from hooks. Mitigation: Replay only hooks flagged 'idempotent' by our hook-compat table and require manual approval otherwise
Risk: Partial finalizer changes could leave resources orphaned. Mitigation: Add a preflight that lists finalizer side-effects and a dry-run mode in the controller API
Risk: Operator image rollout could regress. Mitigation: staged canary rollout to Dedicated, circuit-breaker to roll back operator image automatically if reconciliation error rate > 1% within 10m
